title: 2D Tilemaps - can AI help?
author: loopywolf
selftext:
Hello,

I am looking for an AI that can help me to generate a tileset for a 2D top-down (non-isometric) base-building game.  I will have to make the characters, mobs and a few special pieces myself, but there are a deal of generics I could get help for.   I have hunted far and wide for a tileset, commissioned some others, but had no luck with the rest.

**First Post User History**:

* I used to be a programmer
* I am open minded about AI: I see it as neither evil nor magic.
* I have previous used Claude to help me debug Unity
* Frustrated by the lack of a 2D topdown RTS skeleton on which to base a game, I tried an experiment by asking AI to do it.  (I tried Unity first, but that was a washout, but Claude Code did a great job.)

comments.author: Useful_Use_6170
comments.body: Try Adobe firefly, I like it due to its consistency.

comments.author: pennystudio
comments.body: I had deliberated about this for my second game with Claude. Also a 2D top down game. The conclusion is that although it is a 2D game, it will be easier to make the assets in 3D and just fix the camera angle to look down at it. The reasons is that you don't have to deal with different angle and have different sprite for each assets, unless you want it to be completely flat 2D, with no angle needed (which may look wired for base building). For 3D assets, it's easy to use AI to generate prompt for nano banana 2 to get the concept art in 2D and then use that 2D image in Meshy or Tripo3D to generate the 3D model for it. Once you have the 3D model, you don't have to worry about angle or rotation, it will stay consistent noatter how you want to adjust the camera angle or rotation. Your assets can move freely in the game without looking weird.

comments.author: RatbyteGames
comments.body:
There is a real gap in the market for this. I have tried many approaches and AI is not there yet.

I ended up doing my own top down Hex tile assets for my up coming game:

[Top down hex assets](https://ratbyteboss.itch.io/free-hires-hex-tile-game-assets)

I made them free to try help other indie devs get a head start.
